title: Apple won't refund a $2,700 MacBook that UPS admitted they delivered to the wrong person. What are my options?
comment_text:
I live in Spain, but I ordered a MacBook Pro 14 ($2,662) for my friend who is currently in California for a study semester. It was supposed to be a gift to her.

On Jan 15th, the tracking updated to "Delivered - Met the customer." My friend was home all day, but she never saw a courier, never signed anything, and definitely didn't "meet" anyone. I contacted Apple immediately and they told me they’d look into it. Four days later, I received an email saying their investigation is done and they "won't be providing a refund or a replacement".

I spent two hours on the phone with them and they basically told me their decision is final and I should just "contact the local enforcement".

Here’s where it gets crazy: I pushed UPS to do an actual investigation. They just finished it and **they admitted they messed up.** They confirmed the driver handed it to "someone whose name starts with Q." Nobody at my friend's place has a name starting with Q. Now, the UPS tracking page literally says: *"A claim has been issued to the sender for your package. Please contact the sender for more information."*

So, UPS has basically admitted fault and is ready to pay the claim back to Apple, but Apple is still telling me "No." I’m stuck. I bought a laptop, UPS gave it to a stranger, and Apple is keeping the money and the insurance claim.

Has anyone dealt with this?

1. Since I’m in Spain and she’s in California, who should file the police report? Will Apple even care about a report if I’m the one who files it from abroad?
2. How do I get past the first-level support people? Every time I call, I get someone who just reads a script saying "the decision is final" even though I have proof the carrier admits they failed.
3. I’m terrified of a chargeback because I don’t want my Apple ID  to get blacklisted, but $2,700 is a lot of money to just lose.

Any advice on how to talk to them or who to ask for would be a lifesaver. Thanks in advance.

Wow! Not sure if coincidence or not, but just about an hour after posting this got a new email "We're replacing your items."

title: S25/S25+ owners - initial thoughts?
comment_text:
Just about 24 hours in with my S25+, upgrading from a S20. I've seen threads about the Ultra but not many about the lower two models and curious to know what people are thinking. Some initial thoughts:

* Overall, a solid really nice phone. I'm not one to lament not pushing the boundaries when the basics are so good. My priority is getting a phone that last a long time (hence the only phone with 7 years support and the SD8E) and no reason to believe this won't fit the bill.
* Size is a bit of an adjustment coming from a base model but overall nicer to hold than other large phones like iPhone Pro Max.
* The navy is gorgeous and reflects a variety of light spectrum more than I expected (not sure how else to describe).
* Performance is obviously noticeably better with 5 years better processor but honestly not that night and day.
* I have adjusted to the split notification/quick panels and think I'll keep it that way.
* Fingerprint sensor is very fast and way more accurate than the S20. Just a tap and it's done.
* Turned off most of the AI stuff. The Now brief is "AI" but basically just a basic aggregation of obvious stuff (weather, energy score, calendar) that I'll keep. Found that "AICore" app was using 4GB of storage and cleared that (apparently related to Gemini). It's using less storage now but considering disabling it to see what happens since I don't plan to use Gemini.
* The new AOD that shows background is nice (not sure when they introduced that).
* Smart Switch worked fairly flawless outside of encrypted apps like WhatsApp that needed to be done manually. Up and running within a few hours.
* No OS updates out of the box which was honestly refreshing.

title: 7 Pro to 10 Pro XL - 2nd attempt
comment_text:
I have been generally happy with my Pixel 7 Pro (except for the gradual deterioration of the battery).

  
My main motivation for upgrading to the 10 Pro XL was the insanely good trade-in value for the 7 Pro ($425). I will likely never see such a good deal in the future.

I got the new phone last week and like many others here, found the display showing a marked yellowish tint on any screen with a white background. I tried tuning display settings and saw some limited improvement but still could not get over how bad the whites were. Compared to my 7 Pro it looked weak and watered down. 

Called Google support. They were very helpful and opened a ticket to exchange the phone. I decided to go to the google store in Mountain View to do this in person. The reps at the store were also super helpful. Instead of an exchange, I decided to just return the phone (within the 2 week window), and buy a new one. Both transactions were taken care of with 10 minutes. Walked out feeling hopeful with a new phone.

  
This time around, I am not seeing the yellow tint (or did I just get used to it now???), and by and large the phone seems ok. Maybe I will keep this one.

One bothersome behavior is the momentary blurriness when I close an app. The Google Rep told me this is a feature not a bug! This is the intended behavior of the new UI paradigm in the new pixels. I know engineers like to keep tinkering with things, but Google - Please if it is not broken don't mess with it!!!! Who would ever want this blurring of their UI every time they switch from or exit an app????

The 10 Pro XL does not seem like a major upgrade or improvement over my 3 year old phone though. The 7 Pro had a more appealing and modern design, its curved and slim frame was very stylish, and the display rocked. The 10 Pro XL is a boring slab, with a uninspiring display and nothing else really stands out (I get it that it has a faster processor, tons of AI support etc..).  Have not yet played with the camera and very hopeful this will be the redeeming factor for me.

  
End of the day, the trade-in value for the 7 Pro could be the primary reason I stay with the upgrade.

comment_text:
Hola a todos,

  
Hasta hace dos días he tenido problemas con los audios de WhatsApp y telegram y el sensor de proximidad. Había reiniciado, instalación limpia de iOS, etc y nada. Ayer me puse en contacto con el soporte remoto de Apple y me dieron una instrucciones  ya funciona. Os lo dejo aqu:

  
1° Tener instalado última versión de iOS / WhatsApp / Telegram. 

2° Limpiar bien la parte superior de la pantalla 

3° Ajustes/ WhatsApp y desactivar el micrófono durante 20 segundos. 

4° Reiniciar pero mediante Siri: "oye Siri, reinicia el iPhone"

Una vez reiniciado, entrar a WhatsApp y reproducir un audio. Reproduciendo el audio, lleva el móvil a la oreja como si estuvieras en una llamada. El altavoz principal dejará de sonar y pasará al interno y se apagará la pantalla. 

Me explicó que puede haber un retraso de hasta cinco segundos entre llevarse el móvil a la oreja y la desactivación de la pantalla. Si alejamos el iPhone de la oreja, puede haber otro retraso de hasta cinco segundos teniendo la pantalla negra. Me dijo que para activarla no hay que tocar la pantalla, hay que darle dos o tres veces al botón de bloqueo/desbloqueo.   
A mi me está funcionando perfecto ahora. Me dijo que no es fallo del software ni que el sensor esté roto. Me comentó que es el comportamiento normal de la isla dinámica. A mi me está funcionando bien desde ayer. Espero que sirva de ayuda.

title: One ui 7
comment_text:
It will be a better update than One UI 6 and, certainly, better than 5, because, like it or not, Samsung managed to improve the design. However, I don't feel that enthusiasm that iPhone fans feel when they release a new iOS, and that's frustrating. Samsung isn't changing anything significant, nothing that would really justify a major update.

The Home design is still just a launcher. Animations improve on entry and exit, but ignore overall fluidity. The lock screen is better, but is that it? Typically, Samsung tries to add new features, but ignores refining what already exists. iOS is a consistent system because Apple works to bring few new features, but greatly improves the old ones. We only see Apple facing similar issues as Samsung in giant updates.

I hope Samsung starts to refine the system: fluidity, speed, micro-animations and small details that make the experience more enjoyable. They need to take a break from AI news and focus on the system itself. Before, One UI was good because it offered more customization than pure Android, but now the game is changing.

In summary:

1. Improve the speed of animations and micro-animations.


2. Refine the system to make it faster and more consistent.


3. Solve the problem of screen burn-in.


4. Update the dialog boxes, which are outdated.


5. Make the lock screen more functional.


6. Add features to the home screen (like pressing icons for quick options).


7. Optimize system resource management, which is very volatile today.


8. Enhance dark mode by adjusting contrast and colors for greater consistency.


9. Smarter notifications with efficient grouping and improved quick responses.


10. Customizable navigation gestures, including sensitivity adjustments and specific actions.


11. Improved multitasking, with improvements to split-screen and floating windows.


12. Reduce bloatware or make it easier to remove.


13. Focus on battery savings with power optimization without sacrificing performance.


14. Advanced gaming mode, offering more options and better gaming performance.


15. Integration of the Samsung ecosystem, making connectivity between devices more fluid and cohesive.



If Samsung focuses on these points, it will be able to offer a much more solid and competitive experience, aligning with users' expectations and creating a truly refined and innovative system.

title: I’m losing my mind over iPhone navigation how is this acceptable in 2025?!
comment_text:
I’ve been on iPhone for about 1.5 years now (15 Plus), and every single day I regret switching from Android. Everyone told me iOS was “smooth” and “premium,” but honestly the navigation experience is a complete joke.

First off, the back button. Why the hell is it always in the top-left corner? On a massive phone like the Plus, it’s literally unreachable with one hand. I paid a thousand bucks and I can’t even go back without doing finger gymnastics or using both hands.

Then Apple tried to “fix it” with swipe gestures. Great idea, right? Except you still have to swipe from the absolute left edge of the phone, which is just as awkward on a big screen. And to make it worse, the gesture doesn’t even work everywhere! Some apps have it, some don’t, some are buggy as hell. So half the time you’re just doing trial and error, hoping the gesture decides to work.

And don’t even get me started on Reachability. You want to go back? Now it’s a two-step process: swipe down on the home bar, then tap the back button. How is that better than just having a single universal back button? And half the time Reachability doesn’t even trigger because apps like Spotify, YouTube, or Instagram have bottom nav bars that override the gesture. So you end up pressing some random button instead.

Apple’s excuse is “we don’t want a universal back button because we want to give developers freedom.” Freedom?? Android developers somehow manage just fine with a universal back button, and their apps don’t feel broken. So who is Apple really prioritizing here — the people spending $1,000+ for a so-called premium phone, or the developers who apparently can’t handle consistent navigation rules?

I’m honestly shocked this isn’t a bigger outrage. Navigation is the most basic function of a phone, and on iPhone it feels clunky, inconsistent, and straight up outdated. For a trillion-dollar company, this is embarrassing.

Edit:- talking to a lot of you people I can conclude apple fanboys are inherently dumb Apple would sell you yesterday’s leftovers and you would still call it the future

title: Apple sure does think different [Orange Blob - 2018 15in MacBook Pro]
comment_text:
June 4: Orange dot appears on the bottom left hand corner of my screen. If I poke it, it goes away for a moment. I could kind of move it around but I ruled out a software issue. I thought since I was editing a website at the time, It could have been related to heat from the CPU being exhausted onto the screen. I closed the lid for a while, and came back and it looked normal again.

[https://photos.app.goo.gl/wwTnCmqfso82Z7Ew5](https://photos.app.goo.gl/wwTnCmqfso82Z7Ew5)

June 5: It looked fine for a while, until I started editing photos and the orange dot came back. Again, I could close the lid and it would go away. It didn't really bother me enough to contact Apple at this point. I knew it was going to be a big deal over just an orange inconvenience.

June 6 - June 9: I didn't notice a change, it was still off and on.

June 10: I was traveling with my laptop again. As I always did. Putting it in the padded laptop section of my backpack, Vertical. As most people carry their laptop in a backpack. When I took it out of my bag, the entire very left side of the computer had an orange line down it. The photos don’t do it justice. It looks more obvious in person. (The subtleties of the orange go all the way up to the upper left corner)

[https://photos.app.goo.gl/zS4EArFg3DYVN2qB7](https://photos.app.goo.gl/zS4EArFg3DYVN2qB7)

Since then, this has only appeared to have gotten worse. If I flip my laptop to rest on the right side in my backpack, the orange bar will appear on the right. So it definitely appears side dependent.

So today, June 11: I went to my local Apple store (30 min away) and had them take a look at it. They ran all their hardware diagnostics and physical checks and came back to me saying it was going to be $400 to replace the screen. Which is just unacceptable on a 2 year old computer that cost about $3k , and is meant to be carried around. By the way, the computer looks like it is brand new. Not a scratch or ding on it. It has been very well cared for the 2 years I have had it.

I drove home and called Apple. Hoping over the phone support would be different. And it kind of was! The person I talked with (A senior advisor) was extremely nice and said if I drove back there and asked to speak with the manager that he may be able to pull some strings and get my computer sent in for warranty repair. So, I did just that. I pulled in, talked briefly with their manager who seemed like a nice, but busy, guy. He said that getting this repaired was over his head and I would have to contact Apple support to try and get warranty repair.

So again, I did just that. Before driving home this time, I called Apple support. I spoke with another senior advisor and he also seemed like a very nice guy. He talked with my local Apple store for about 10 minutes and returned to my call saying the best they could do is a $400 screen replacement. They couldn't even offer me a discount because Apple service isn't “itemized” so they can't just deduct the cost of labor or parts. (seems pretty planned to me)

My worry is the orange blob is just going to keep getting worse. But I'm more upset with Apple customer support. I get that It only had a 1 year warranty, but why is a $3k computer only designed to last a year? A 1 year warranty is supposed to cover factory defects that you would catch within the first year. But what if it's a problem that takes more than a year to show? And that's what Apple seems to be counting on. Then they just turn around and tell you its end user damage when it's really just a design flaw.

And if you look up “Orange Blob/smudge” followed by “macbook” you will find articles dating back to 2010, all with the same issue as me. I'm hoping to at least start some conversation and have some people reach out with their issues regarding this so I have some leverage saying it's not just me.

(Hopefully I'm posting this in the right place. As this isn't tech support, and it's only calling out a major hardware flaw I don't see this intruding on any rules.)
